rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the heavens, earth, and all within them, and has prescribed mercy for Himself.
rows.anchor: يخبر تعالى أنه مالك السموات والأرض ومن فيهن، وأنه قد كتب على نفسه المقدسة الرحمة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound report says God wrote above the Throne that His mercy prevails over His wrath.
rows.anchor: قال النبي (3) صلى الله عليه وسلم "إن الله لما خلق الخلق كتب كتابا عنده فوق العرش، إن رحمتي تغلب غضبي"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “He will surely gather you” introduces an oath: God swears to gather His servants at the appointed Resurrection, which believers do not doubt.
rows.anchor: هذه اللام هي الموطئة للقسم، فأقسم بنفسه الكريمة ليجمعن عباده لميقات يوم معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deny the gathering remain uncertain and wavering about it.
rows.anchor: فأما الجاحدون المكذبون فهم (1) في ريبهم (2) يترددون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet affirmed water at the standing before God, with believers reaching prophets’ pools and angels driving unbelievers away.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الوقوف بين يدي رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls Ibn Mardawayh’s report about the pools an unusual report.
rows.anchor: يذودون الكفار عن حياض الأنبياء". هذا حديث غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports that every prophet has a basin, they vie over its visitors, and Muhammad hopes to have the most visitors.
rows.anchor: وفي الترمذي: "إن لكل نبي حوضا، وإنهم يتباهون أيهم أكثر واردة، وأرجو أن أكون أكثرهم واردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who lose themselves are those who do not believe in resurrection or fear the evil of that day.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يصدقون بالمعاد، ولا يخافون شر ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every creature in heaven and earth belongs to God and remains under His dominion, governance, and control; there is no deity but Him.
rows.anchor: الجميع عباده وخلقه، وتحت قهره وتصرفه وتدبيره، ولا (7) إله إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears His servants’ words and knows their movements, thoughts, and secrets.
rows.anchor: السميع لأقوال عباده، العليم بحركاتهم وضمائرهم وسرائرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to take no protector except God, the sole creator and originator of the heavens and earth without precedent.
rows.anchor: لا أتخذ وليا إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، فإنه فاطر السموات والأرض، أي: خالقهما ومبدعهما على غير مثال سبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command echoes the rebuke of those who urge worship of another deity.
rows.anchor: كما قال {قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون} [الزمر: 64]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier communities were afflicted with poverty and straitened livelihoods, as well as illness, sickness, and pain, so that they might humble themselves in supplication.
rows.anchor: يعني: الفقر والضيق في العيش {والضراء} وهي الأمراض والأسقام والآلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the affliction came, they should have pleaded humbly, but their hearts neither softened nor became humble.
rows.anchor: فهلا إذ ابتليناهم بذلك تضرعوا إلينا وتمسكنوا إلينا (2) {ولكن قست قلوبهم} أي: ما رقت ولا خشعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan made their shirk and sins seem attractive to them.
rows.anchor: وزين لهم الشيطان ما كانوا يعملون} أي: من الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting the admonition means turning away from it, neglecting it, and putting it behind their backs.
rows.anchor: أي: أعرضوا عنه وتناسوه وجعلوه وراء ظهورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening every door means granting every kind of provision they chose; this is divine enticement and respite.
rows.anchor: أي: فتحنا عليهم أبواب الرزق من كل ما يختارون، وهذا (3) استدراج منه تعالى وإملاء لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they rejoiced in wealth, children, and provisions, God seized them suddenly, leaving them despairing of all good.
rows.anchor: من الأموال والأولاد والأرزاق {أخذناهم بغتة} أي: على غفلة {فإذا هم مبلسون} أي: آيسون من كل خير

rows.speaker: الولبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Walibi reports Ibn Abbas’s gloss that al-mublis means one who despairs.
rows.anchor: قال الوالبي، عن ابن عباس: المبلس: الآيس

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan warns that people with ease who do not fear divine plotting, or people under restriction who miss God’s watchfulness, lack judgment; he says God gave a people their wish and then seized them.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: مكر بالقوم ورب الكعبة؛ أعطوا حاجتهم ثم أخذوا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God’s command surprised the people during their heedless luxury; do not feel secure from God, for only the wicked do.
rows.anchor: وما أخذ الله قوما قط إلا عند سكرتهم وغرتهم ونعيمهم (4) فلا تغتروا بالله

rows.speaker: مالك عن الزهري
rows.claim: Malik reports al-Zuhri’s interpretation of the opened doors as the ease and concealment of worldly life.
rows.anchor: قال مالك، عن الزهري: {فتحنا عليهم أبواب كل شيء} قال: إرخاء (5) الدنيا وسترها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that worldly gifts a sinner receives in line with his desires are gradual enticement, and recites this verse.
rows.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا رأيت الله يعطي العبد من الدنيا على معاصيه ما يحب، فإنما هو استدراج"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit the Prophet’s warning about worldly gifts to sinners through Harma and Ibn Luhaia from Uqba ibn Muslim, from Uqba ibn Amir.
rows.anchor: ورواه ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم، من حديث حرملة وابن لهيعة، عن عقبة بن مسلم، عن عقبة بن عامر

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubada reports that the Prophet said God grants moderation and chastity when He wills a people’s continuance or growth, but opens a door of treachery when He wills their ruin.
rows.anchor: عن إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة، عن عبادة بن الصامت [رضي الله عنه] (2) أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden seizure of the wrongdoers concludes with their destruction, as the next verse states.
rows.anchor: كما قال: {فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا والحمد لله رب العالمين}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says polytheists urged believers to follow their way and abandon Muhammad’s religion; the parable portrays one who turns back to unbelief after guidance as a lost traveler lured by devils while companions on Islam’s path call him back.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: قال المشركون للمؤمنين: اتبعوا سبيلنا، واتركوا دين محمد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses “the devils made him lose his way” as their leading him astray, linking the verb to the phrase about people inclining toward them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {استهوته الشياطين في الأرض} أضلته في الأرض، يعني: استهوته (1) مثل قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ali ibn Abi Talha, compares idol worship to a desert caller who leads the lost traveler to destruction, while the companions’ call to the road guides him safely.
rows.anchor: علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {قل أندعو من دون الله ما لا ينفعنا ولا يضرنا}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The parable’s desert callers are ghouls who call a person by his name and ancestry; following idols likewise ends in ruin and regret after seeming meaningful.
rows.anchor: وهذه الداعية التي تدعو في البرية من الغيلان، يقول: مثل من يعبد هذه الآلهة من دون الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the parable is a confused man whose companions summon him to the path, like someone who strays after having been guided.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران} قال: رجل حيران يدعوه أصحابه إلى الطريق

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi reports Ibn Abbas’s view that the man disobeys God and follows Satan, while his human allies call him to what they mistakenly claim is guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {كالذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران} هو الذي لا يستجيب لهدى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects this reading because the verse explicitly says the companions call to guidance, which cannot be misguidance after God calls it guidance.
rows.anchor: وهذا خلاف ظاهر الآية؛ فإن الله أخبر أن أصحابه يدعونه إلى الهدى، فغير جائز أن يكون ضلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir agrees with Ibn Jarir: the confused, misguided man has companions on the clear path calling him to join them, but he refuses; God could guide him back.
rows.anchor: وهو كما قال ابن جرير، وكان (5) سياق الآية يقتضي أن هذا الذي استهوته الشياطين في الأرض حيران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assertion that God’s guidance is the only guidance echoes that none can mislead one whom God guides.
rows.anchor: كما قال: {ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل} (1) [الزمر: 37]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide those He leaves astray, and they have no helpers; the verse then commands exclusive submission to Him.
rows.anchor: إن تحرص على هداهم فإن الله لا يهدي من يضل وما لهم من ناصرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Submission to the Lord of all worlds means devoting worship exclusively to Him.
rows.anchor: أي: نخلص له العباد (2) وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrated Hour begins with a quake that rocks earth like a ship in rough seas; people panic, demons flee and are driven back by angels, and all seek refuge without protection.
rows.anchor: ثم ترتج الأرض بأهلها رجة فتكون كالسفينة المرمية (4) في البحر، تضربها الأمواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the earth splits and the sky becomes molten, the stars scatter and the sun and moon are eclipsed.
rows.anchor: فرأوا أمرا عظيما لم يروا مثله، وأخذهم لذلك من الكرب والهول ما الله به عليم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says the dead know nothing of the upheaval; when Abu Huraira asks about those excepted from the blast, he identifies the martyrs, whom God protects and sustains.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الأموات لا يعلمون بشيء من ذلك" قال أبو هريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour’s quake also matches the warning that nursing mothers are distracted and pregnant women miscarry; the people remain in this prolonged torment as long as God wills.
rows.anchor: قال: وهو الذي يقول الله، عز وجل: {يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the blast of death, all in the heavens and earth die except those God wills; God then causes Gabriel, Michael, the Throne-bearers, and finally the Angel of Death to die, leaving Himself alone.
rows.anchor: فيصعق أهل السموات [وأهل] (1) الأرض إلا من شاء الله، فإذا هم قد خمدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With God alone remaining, the heavens and earth are folded, then spread out again as a level plain, fulfilling the cited verses.
rows.anchor: طوى السموات والأرض طي السجل للكتب (7) ثم دحاهما ثم يلقفهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raises the dead in the changed earth by sending water and forty days of rain until bodies regrow; souls are then gathered and cast into the trumpet.
rows.anchor: ثم يأمر الله الأجساد أن تنبت فتنبت كنبات الطراثيث -أو: كنبات البقل -حتى إذا تكاملت أجسادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the resurrection blast, souls return to bodies and people emerge barefoot and naked to a single long stand, weeping and seeking an intercessor; Adam and the other prophets decline until Muhammad is granted intercession to begin judgment.
rows.anchor: ثم يأمر الله إسرافيل أن ينفخ نفخة البعث، فينفخ نفخة البعث، فتخرج الأرواح كأنها النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet describes successive ranks of angels descending in great numbers and lighting the earth; each rank says God is still coming.
rows.anchor: ثم ينزل [من] (15) أهل السماء الثانية بمثلي من نزل من الملائكة، وبمثلي من فيها من الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God descends amid clouds and angels; eight angels carry the Throne, glorifying Him, as He tells humans and jinn their deeds and records will be read and each person must answer for them.
rows.anchor: في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة، فيحمل عرشه (16) يومئذ ثمانية -وهم اليوم أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell brings forth a dark neck and God reminds Adam’s children that Satan is their enemy and that they were commanded to worship Him; the quoted warning says many were led astray.
rows.anchor: ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان إنه لكم عدو مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All nations kneel before their books; God judges even animals, including settling the hornless animal’s claim against the horned, then turns them to dust, prompting the disbeliever’s wish to be dust.
rows.anchor: وترى كل أمة جاثية كل أمة تدعى إلى كتابها اليوم تجزون ما كنتم تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment begins with bloodshed: a martyr who fought for God is affirmed and sent to Paradise, while killings and wrongs are otherwise subject to requital, punishment, or mercy.
rows.anchor: فكان أول ما يقضي فيه الدماء، ويأتي كل قتيل في سبيل الله، عز وجل، ويأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A non-martyr’s killer admits seeking honor for himself; God condemns him, and every killing and injustice is subject to requital, punishment, or mercy.
rows.anchor: فيقول: يا رب، قتلتهم لتكون العزة لك ولي. فيقول: تعست. ثم لا تبقى نفس قتلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God settles all remaining wrongs, down to requiring a seller who diluted milk with water to separate the milk from the water.
rows.anchor: حتى إنه ليكلف شائب اللبن بالماء ثم يبيعه أن يخلص اللبن من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A herald orders people to follow what they worshipped; Jews and Christians follow angels appearing as Ezra and Jesus, and their gods lead them to Hell, as the cited verse says.
rows.anchor: ويجعل يومئذ ملك من الملائكة على صورة عزير، ويجعل ملك من الملائكة على صورة عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers refuse false gods and recognize God when He reveals His shin; believers prostrate, while hypocrites cannot and their backs stiffen.
rows.anchor: فيكشف لهم عن ساقه، ويتجلى لهم من عظمته ما يعرفون أنه ربهم، فيخرون سجدا على وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sets the bridge over Hell, sharp as a blade and fitted with hooks and thorns; people cross at differing speeds, some safely, some injured, and some falling face-first into Hell.
rows.anchor: ويضرب الله الصراط بين ظهراني جهنم كحد الشفرة -أو: كحد السيف -عليه كلاليب وخطاطيف وحسك
